spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the explainer's writing-mode resolution step with the shipped logical scroll-snap-align surface, and presents the physical hand-off table exactly as the proposal defines it.

interactive.rationale: Writing-mode and alignment button groups restyle a real two-axis snap scroller, and the measure button performs a physical nudge with a numeric settle readout.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises flipping writing modes and watching the alignment move between physical axes; the measured readout shows precisely that (240×170 vs 170×240 cells).

edge_cases.rationale: Covers vertical-rl/vertical-lr and the center/end no-boundary caveat honestly, but cross-writing-mode scroller nesting (inner vertical-rl inside horizontal outer) is only described in the table since the hand-off itself is unshipped.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5086608215900160, the explainer's writing-mode section, and the css-scroll-snap-1 scroll-snap-align definition.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's control and propagation assertions pin the measurable contracts; the resolution behaviour shown here rides on the shipped scroll-snap-align surface those assertions exercise.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud fallback, no chrome-devtools-mcp): horizontal-tb start settled 240/170 on boundaries; vertical-rl rendered 170×240 cells and settled scrollLeft 0 / scrollTop 240, both on boundaries with swapped axes; center mode correctly reported no boundary verdict; zero console errors; both viewports screenshotted.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the boundary measurement for start alignment, a labelled no-snap fallback, and a measure-ran assert for non-start alignments.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; highlighted hand-off cells use accent-blue text on stone/paper at AA+; buttons 44px with outline-based pressed state.

accessibility.rationale: Button groups are labelled, the scroller is keyboard-focusable with an aria-label, the readout is role=status aria-live=polite, and the hand-off table has a caption and header scopes.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×800: scroller is width-clamped (min(100%,420px)), zero document overflow, measurements identical.

openQuestions.title: Build the nested cross-writing-mode hand-off rig once the feature ships
openQuestions.detail: The physical hand-off across differing writing modes (vertical-rl lane inside horizontal-tb feed) is currently only explained, because no shipping engine runs the propagation step. When SingleAxisScrollContainersForScrollSnap is testable, add a measured rig proving the ancestor applies the propagated axis in its own physical space regardless of the lane's writing mode.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel toggle buttons no horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsic/clamped sizing (min(), fit-content) before fixed widths so layouts survive narrow viewports.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The snap scroller uses width: min(100%, 420px) and the measure logic reads rendered cell rects instead of assuming fixed physical dimensions.

guidanceConsulted.query: scroll snap carousel accessible keyboard scrolling
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Derive snap state from settled positions/native events rather than assumptions.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The readout reports measured settle offsets against measured cell geometry per writing mode, which caught and fixed an initial physical-moduli bug.

summary: Logical-to-physical snap resolution driven live: the same scroll-snap-align declaration measured snapping x/y in horizontal-tb and swapped axes in vertical-rl (cells 240×170 → 170×240), with the unshipped ancestor hand-off honestly presented as explanation plus a follow-up rig question. Cloud headless Chromium 141 verification, both viewports clean.
